summary: An L-4 cab on a stone base above Buffalo, Wyoming, approved in 1941 but not finished until 1950; staffed only in emergencies, now a popular Recreation.gov rental.

facts.design: L-4 cab on 10-foot stone base, with catwalk

access.note: Overnight rental via Recreation.gov, June 15-October 20, snow permitting; $50/night reported in 2024 news coverage.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Bighorn National Forest

events.note: Construction plans approved in 1941, before the cab itself was built.
Lookout completed. A tourism listing and a reprint newspaper piece attribute construction to the CCC, but the Civilian Conservation Corps had been disbanded by 1942, so that attribution is doubtful.
Occupied as a fire lookout until 'the early 1970s' per the Recreation.gov listing; exact year not given.

notes_for_editor: A travel-blog page (roadtripryan.com) and the WebSearch AI summary both offered a vivid, specific narrative - an 1922 primitive fire watch predecessor and a 1938 lightning strike that set the lookout's bed on fire - that appears nowhere in the NHLR register, the FFLA register, or the Forest Service's own Bighorn lookouts history page. I did not use any of that material; it has the hallmarks of AI-generated filler rather than sourced history, and a human may want to track down the roadtripryan.com page's own citations if any exist. Note that the CCC-construction claim itself is NOT part of that invented narrative - Recreation.gov and the Rocket-Miner newspaper piece (sources 4 and 6, both used in the story) independently and directly state the lookout was 'Constructed in 1950 by the Civilian Conservation Corps,' so that part is sourced, just flagged in the story as doubtful because the CCC was disbanded in 1942. A footnote error was also fixed: the story had attributed the 'Emergency' staffing status to 'the Forest Fire Lookout Association's own register,' but that fact actually comes from firelookout.com, an independent reference site by Rex Kamstra, not from FFLA's own site (firelookout.org, source 3) - the FFLA page for Wyoming is just a name/county/status table with no staffing field for this lookout. Text corrected; footnote [^2] was already pointing at the right source. The record's elevation_m (2911.8m / ~9554ft) runs a little low against the 9600-9610ft the registers give; likely just rounding/survey differences, not flagged as a correction. No other conflicts found worth a formal correction.
